text:
alice.dev: heads up — seeing a steady eviction spiral in eu-west1 over the last 2 hrs. lots of tiny gpu pods (1g) getting preempted and rescheduled across racks. graphs: CPU ok, GPU util low, pending pods spike.
ben_platform: any recent scheduler changes or taint/affinity rollouts?
dmitri_scheduler: no scheduler rollout in the last day. looks like the anti-affinity rule + rack-level taint is causing tiny pods to scatter. they then trigger binpack backfill on other racks -> churn.
alice.dev: exact symptoms: pods get placed on rack-a, then a canary batch moves some larger jobs to that rack, tiny pods evicted, reschedule to rack-b, repeat. eviction rate ~15/min.
carla_sre: got the alert from infra-bot too. infra-bot: "alert: gpu_eviction_rate > 10/min in eu-west1 for 130m" :rotating_light:
raj_infra: cost note — the scatter increases cross-AZ egress for checkpoint pulls occasionally, ups our networking bills when jobs pull shared model shards. also more spot spills.
ben_platform: root cause hypothesis: packing heuristics currently prefer AZ spread for redundancy. for small-gpu workloads that increases fragmentation. propose a new policy that prefers GPU-type consolidation at rack level for <=2g pods.
dmitri_scheduler: agreed. quick experiment: change priority plugin weight to favor node-similarity for pods with label "small-gpu=true". sample k8s-scheduler config snippet:
```
policy: "binpack-consolidate"
predicates:
  - name: PodFitsResources
  - name: NoScheduleTaints
priorities:
  - name: NodeAffinityPriority
    weight: 3
  - name: ResourceConsolidation
    weight: 25
```

ben_platform: ^^ we should canary that in eu-west1-dev first. also add a descheduler rule to avoid long-term imbalance.
carla_sre: will schedule canary. request: add metrics for "consolidation_hits" and eviction_reason tag to downstream dashboards.
alice.dev: I can add a small eval that uses realistic tiny-gpu mix to reproduce.
raj_infra: remember to include cost delta estimate. consolidation may increase rack-local contention for large jobs — need fallback to current policy when tail latency of critical jobs rises.
dmitri_scheduler: plan: 1) deploy scheduler policy change to eu-west1-dev (canary) 2) enable descheduler evict rule with "ConsolidateSmallGPU" 3) monitor: eviction_rate, pod_start_latency, network_egress, large-job-p95 4) rollback if large-job-p95 > baseline + 10%
carla_sre: I'll create the canary ticket and chart panel. tagging @oncall for a heads-up.
infra-bot: "canary created: eu-west1-dev-scheduler-3876543210; tests queued"
canary-bot: "test-run: consolidation-policy-smoke, status: queued; ETA ~12m"
ben_platform: also add a short-lived feature flag so we can toggle "consolidate_small_gpu" without redeploy.
alice.dev: thanks — if canary looks good i'll prod to staging then prod. will post quick results here. :thumbsup:
